Derive the relation between different Einstein Coefficients at thermal equilibrium.
Discuss the nature of emission for hf < < KT.

A quantum simple harmonic oscillator consists of an electron bounded by a restoring force
proportional to its displacement relative to an equilibrium position. The photon of 550 nm is used to
excite the oscillator to its first excited state from the ground state. Calculate the proportionality
constant and energy of the first excited state.

State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. 'At room temperature the
probability of finding an electron at the Fermi level is 0.5',

With the help of schematic diagram describe how the Davisson-Germer experiment confirmed the
wave nature of electrons.

A 30 eV electron and proton are incident on a square barrier of height 40 eV. What is the probability
that the electron and proton will tunnel through the barrier if its width is 0.10 nm.

State whether the wavefunction 
 is physically acceptable or not in
the finite potential well with finite height 'U' and length 'L'. Justify your answer.
Derive an expression for density-of-states.

The frequency of photon that causes v = 0 to v = 1 transition in the CO molecule is 6.42 x 1013 Hz.
Ignore any changes in the rotational energy.
(a) Calculate the force constant k for this molecule.
(b) What is the maximum classical amplitude of vibration for this molecule in the v = 0 vibrational
state 
.

The Fermi level in silver is 5.5 eV at zero kelvin. Calculate the number of free electrons per unit
volume.

What are the factors on which the electric field at some point P near a dipole in a dielectric material
depends? Obtain a relationship between the polarizability and the relative permittivity of dielectric
materials.

The atomic weight of Si is 28 and has a density of 2.33 g cm−3 and each atom has polarizability of 2
×10-40 F m2. Calculate the ratio of internal field to external field in the case of Si. Given ε0 = 8.854
×10 -12 F/m.

State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. "The density of states in
a bulk material can be obtained using quantum free electron theory because the energy levels of
electrons are treated as continuous."
What are biomaterials? Explain its various biomedical applications with suitable examples.

Explain how nanotechnology is applied in microelectronics, optoelectronics and medical
applications.

State whether the given statement is true or false and justify your answer. "The electrical resistivity
of metallic glasses is high and remains almost constant with temperature."

Explain with a suitable diagram the construction and working principle of a semiconductor laser.

An optic fibre of core refractive index 1.80 is to be cladded to ensure that the refracted light ray
grazes the interface. The optical fibre will contain light travelling within 10° of the fibre axis when it
is placed in air medium. What minimum refractive index is allowed for the cladding? If the same
optical fiber is placed in water medium (refractive index of water = 1.33), then find out the
acceptance angle and numerical aperture.

What is modal dispersion? Which type of optical fibre can be used to remove this kind of
dispersion?

Define (i) group speed and (ii) phase speed. Show that for a given non-relativistic quantum particle,
the group speed of a wave packet is equal to the particle speed.

When a free electron scatters a 0.854 nm x-ray photon, the electron recoils with a speed of 1.48×
106 m/s. What is the resulting Compton shift in the photon's wavelength?

Obtain the general solution to the Schrödinger equation for a particle of mass m in a finite potential
well of height U and length L. Mention the boundary conditions to solve this system. Sketch the
probability density for the lowest two energy states.

A student conducted a photoelectric effect experiment by shining light of various wavelengths onto
a metal surface. To stop the flow of photocurrent, the student applied a negative potential until the
current dropped to zero. The following readings were recorded. Are these readings valid? Provide
justification for your answer.

Increasing the mass of a particle enhances its tunneling probability for a fixed barrier. State
whether the given statement is True or False. Justify your answer.

Explain the phenomenon of single-particle interference with reference to the double-slit experiment.
Illustrate your answer with suitable diagrams and discuss how this experiment demonstrates the
probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics and the principle of superposition.
What are Bell states, and how do they illustrate the concept of quantum entanglement?

The S gate changes the probability of measuring a qubit in the computational basis.
State whether the given statement is True or False. Justify your answer.

Explain the working principles of the CNOT and CCNOT gates with the help of circuit diagrams and
truth tables.

junction solar cell".

Write the assumptions made in Planck's hypothesis of blackbody radiation. How Planck's law succeeds in explaining the
short and long wavelength regions of radiation.

Explain how the surface to volume ratio influences the different properties of materials with examples.
Explain top-down and bottom-up approach for preparation of nanomaterial using schematic diagram.

Illustrate the different types of optical fibres based on their refractive index profiles. Discuss the
communication application of optical fiber with block diagram.

An atom has two energy levels with a transition wavelength of 582 nm. At 300 K, 4.0 x 1020 atoms
are in the lower state. (a) How many occupy the upper state under conditions of thermal
equilibrium? (b) Suppose, instead, that 7.0 x 1020 atoms are pumped into upper state, with 4.0 x
1020 atoms in the lower state. How much energy could be released in a single laser pulse?

If a laser medium has a very short excited-state lifetime, how does it affect laser action? Justify your
answer.

Analyze the relationship between the scattering angle and the wavelength shift when the target
metal is exposed to extremely intense and monochromatic electromagnetic radiation and discuss
the physical significance of the Compton effect.

In an experiment, the tungsten cathode which has a threshold of 435 nm is irradiated by ultraviolet
light of wavelength 215 nm. Calculate (i) maximum energy of emitted photoelectrons, and (ii) work
function for tungsten (in eV).

If the frequency of incident radiation is increased beyond the threshold while intensity is kept
constant, what happens to:
(i) The number of emitted electrons, and
(ii) Their kinetic energy?

Solve the Schrodinger equation for a particle of mass m in a one-dimensional infinite potential well
(box) of length L and obtain an expression for wavefunction of the particle.

A student conducted an experiment on the photoelectric effect by shining light with a wavelength of
500 nm onto a metal surface. To stop the flow of photocurrent, the student applied a negative
potential until the current dropped to zero. He repeated the experiment by varying the distance of
the light source (with no other changes made to the experimental setup). How do these variations
in distance affect the stopping potential and photocurrent? Justify your answer.

Well-1 and Well-2 are two square wells having same length. Well-1 has walls of finite height, and
well-2 has walls of infinite height. Both the wells contain identical quantum particles, one in each
well. Compare the magnitude of the ground-state momentum.

For the quantum circuit shown below, identify the output for each of the computational basis states
(|00⟩, |01⟩, |10⟩, |11⟩) as the input.
Based on the obtained output, draw the equivalent two-qubit gate for the above quantum circuit.
Explain Bloch sphere representation of a qubit.

Both the set of all complex column matrices of order (n × 1) and the set of all complex row
matrices of order (1 × n) form linear vector spaces (LVS) over the field of complex numbers.
State whether the given statement is True or False. Justify your answer.
Explain the postulates of Quantum Mechanics.
Show that the SWAP gate/circuit interchanges the state of the two qubits.

A three level laser emits light of wavelength 550 nm. (a) What is the ratio of population of the upper
level (E2) to that of the lower level (E1) in laser transition, at 300 K? (b) At what temperature the
ratio of the population of E2 to that of E1 becomes half?

A ruby laser emits light at a wavelength of 694.4 nm. If a laser pulse is emitted for 12.0 ps and the
energy release per pulse is 150 mJ, what is the length of the pulse, and how many photons are
there in each pulse?

Define (i) group speed and (ii) phase speed of a wave packet. Show that the group speed of a wave
packet is equal to the particle speed for a free non- relativistic quantum particle.

Molybdenum has a work function of 4.2 eV.
i) Find the cut off wavelength and cut off frequency for the photoelectric effect.
ii) What is the stopping potential if the incident light has wavelength of 180 nm? (1 eV = 1.6x10-19 J
and h=6.63x10-34 J-s)
Illustrate the de Broglie concept of wave properties of particles.

Apply the Schrödinger equation to a particle in a one-dimensional "box" of length L and obtain the
energy values of the particle.

The J = 0 to J = 1 rotational transition of the CO molecule occurs at a frequency of 1.15 x 1011Hz.
Page 1 of 3
Use this information to;
i) Calculate the moment of inertia of the molecule.
ii) Calculate the bond-length of the molecule.
iii) What happens if another photon of frequency 1.15 x 1011 Hz is incident on the CO molecule
while it is in the J = 1 state?

A proton in a one-dimensional box has an energy of 400 keV in its first excited state. How wide is
the box?
Explain atomic, ionic, orientational and space charge polarizability using suitable diagram.

Consider a semiconductor in the form of a rectangular strip of thickness 10 µm. Let a current of 1
mA flow along its length and a transverse magnetic field of strength 1T be applied across its
thickness. If charge carrier density is 3.1 x 1023 m-3, then calculate Hall coefficient and Hall voltage.

Explain why ferroelectrics are known as non-linear dielectrics. Sketch the ferroelectric hysteresis
loop.
Explain metallic glass. Write any two property and applications of metallic glass.
Obtain an expression for rotational energy of a diatomic molecule.

Calculate the surface to volume ratio of a spherical body which has radius of 100 nm.
